_comment: YOLO models of the Axelera Voyager SDK model zoo that SustainML offers for CNNs on the Axelera board.
reference: accuracy (COCO mAP etc., fp32 and the int8 loss) and FPS published by Axelera for the PCIe card.
measured: on our Axelera Edge 130p and from the model's ONNX file (onnx_url), see "measurement":
latency_s      time of one inference, one input processed alone, as for every hardware in SustainML
chip_fps       in the same runs, inferences per second of the chip alone (dev FPS): 1 / chip_fps is the chip's time per inference
full_load_fps  inferences per second with all AIPU cores busy (the board's throughput)
memory_mb      weights_mb + working_mb, computed as for every model in SustainML (model_memory.py)
power_w        null: this board revision has no power sensor, so yolo_catalog.resources() estimates it
null values are placeholders that yolo_catalog.resources() fills, saying so in its "source".
import_measurements.py puts new measurements in this file.
sdk_version: 1.7.0 (measurements); model zoo of SDK 1.7.0/1.8.0 (identical for these 36 models)

object-detection.description: Find and classify objects in an image or video frame, returning an axis-aligned bounding box, class and confidence for each one (people, vehicles, animals, everyday objects).
object-detection.outputs: bounding boxes, class labels, confidence scores
object-detection.classes: 80 everyday object classes (person, car, bus, bicycle, dog, cup, ...)

oriented-object-detection.description: Detect objects with rotated (oriented) bounding boxes, for objects seen from above at any angle such as in aerial, drone or satellite images (planes, ships, vehicles, storage tanks).
oriented-object-detection.outputs: rotated bounding boxes, class labels, confidence scores
oriented-object-detection.classes: 15 aerial classes (plane, ship, storage tank, harbor, bridge, large/small vehicle, ...)

instance-segmentation.description: Detect each object and outline it with a pixel mask, separating individual instances of the same class (each person, each car).
instance-segmentation.outputs: per-object pixel masks, bounding boxes, class labels, confidence scores

semantic-segmentation.description: Label every pixel of a street or driving scene with its class (road, sidewalk, car, person, building, vegetation, sky), without separating individual objects.

keypoint-detection.description: Estimate human body pose: detect each person and locate their body keypoints (nose, eyes, shoulders, elbows, wrists, hips, knees, ankles).
keypoint-detection.outputs: person bounding boxes and 17 body keypoints per person

measurement.board: Axelera Edge 130p, AXE-BME20P1AE16A02 Rev 1.1, 1x Metis AIPU (4 cores, 800 MHz, INT8), PCIe Gen3 x4, 16 GB
measurement.host: Dell Pro Slim Plus XE5, Intel Core Ultra 7 265, 32 GB RAM, Ubuntu 24.04
measurement.software: Voyager SDK 1.7.0, Metis driver 1.5.5, card firmware 1.8.0 (runtime 1.7.0), board controller 7.4
measurement.latency: one input processed alone: axrunmodel build/<model>/<model>/1/model.json --seconds 10 --aipu-cores 1 --no-double-buffer, latency = 1 / system FPS (includes the PC-to-card transfer), mean of the runs. Measured 2026-11-10, all 36 models. The chip time (dev FPS) was the same in every run; the spread between runs (up to 15 %) is on the PC side
measurement.full_load: all 4 AIPU cores, one copy of the model each, with double buffering: axrunmodel build/<model>/<model>/1/model.json --seconds 10, 3 runs, mean system FPS. Measured 2026-11-03 to 2026-11-06, all 36 models. Used for frame-rate requirements, not as the latency
measurement.memory: model_memory.onnx_memory_mb() of the model's ONNX file at its input resolution: weights plus the peak working memory of one input, floating-point values at 32 bits
measurement.power: not measured: the Edge 130p Rev 1.1 has no power sensor (axmonitor cannot read it; Axelera recommends a wall meter, P_run - P_idle). Datasheet: typical 8-15 W running DNNs at maximum performance at 25 C, TDP 19 W

placeholders.latency_s: the full-load time per inference (1 / full_load_fps, else 1 / the reference FPS) times the mean ratio latency_s x full_load_fps of the models measured both ways
placeholders.power_w: estimate: the datasheet typical power of axelera_devices.yaml (midpoint, 11.5 W) x the share of the latency the chip computes, (1 / chip_fps) / latency_s, as CarbonTracker does for devices it cannot read (watts x utilization). Without chip_fps, the datasheet midpoint alone
